source_record.title: Backup filenames collide within a second and WITH FORMAT can overwrite prior backup
source_record.trigger_and_safe_repro_design: Two authorized backups of same database/directory choose timestamps within same UTC second; paths identical. Later BACKUP ... FORMAT can replace earlier backup media. Records now share file; retention of one may delete another supposedly preserved file. Never execute this against user backup files; deterministic path function test sufficient.
source_record.root_cause: Second-resolution timestamp treated as unique filename; no GUID/exclusive reservation. Retention reasons over records not unique physical paths.
source_record.correction_design: Use collision-resistant unique ID in filename and prohibit overwriting existing destination; preserve record-to-file identity. Retention should validate canonical distinct paths and never delete a file referenced by retained record.
source_record.regression_tests: Same-time parallel name generation unique; simulated same destination refused; pruning duplicate path references preserves retained valid backup. Isolated SQL integration later with explicit permission.
source_record.counterevidence_and_limits: SQL concurrency might make one backup fail instead of overwrite; either violates no-collision claim. Exact physical media behavior not runtime tested. Scheduled/interactive callers can overlap.

independent_challenge.reasoning: Filename contains only database and UTC timestamp to seconds; two authorized same-directory requests in same second choose same path, regardless distinct row GUID. BACKUP WITH FORMAT permits media replacement. Simultaneous SQL calls can instead fail; no particular concurrency outcome asserted. Sequential short backups can collide too. Retention protects newest valid record ID but does not deduplicate underlying paths, so duplicate records undermine file identity protection.
independent_challenge.counterevidence: Destination requires authorized backup actor/configured directory, SQL permissions and actual engine file access. COPY_ONLY preserves external backup-chain semantics; values parameterized and database identifier validated. No anonymous SQL injection claim.
